algorithm: Complex convolution resampling of a regular 64×64 image at 64 irregular points, using an 8×8 subpixel table of 32×32 complex kernels and zero extension outside the image. Each point has 32 lane-wise x contributions and a 32-lane sum reduction.
mapping: Native/CUDA.jl 32×8 threads and two blocks; each warp processes four points. Native warp shuffle tree uses no shared memory. KA/JACC emulate the same lane dataflow using 512 Float64 shared slots and 44 block barriers per block.

reference_audit.finding: Historical CUDA.jl already implements the complex convolution and native warp reduction. It uses Float64 floor/bins instead of native floorf, guards image loads before bounds rather than using padded source storage, and sorts by kernel sub-bin order rather than the native swapped-axis locality key. These are precision/input/memory mapping differences, not evidence of a wrong configured scientific operator. Named adapter aligns Float32 floorf and fully initialized padded storage.
reference_audit.named_configuration: Guarded-header macros NPOINTS64 IMG_SIZE64 GCF_DIM32 REPEAT3; GCF_GRID8 and 32×8 source geometry retained. Two generated dyadic fixtures replace source default random/transcendental inputs.
reference_audit.point_sort_scope: Named comparator uses floor fractions and swapped-axis key. It agrees with source modf comparator for nonnegative points, but differs for negative coordinates included here. The study_common source comment about native ordering is qualified by this statement. All four consume the same complete serialized ordered point list.

observation: The operator is complex resampling from a regular grid at irregular coordinates, with a subpixel convolution table. A delta-kernel fixture provides an independent image-sampling identity, while scaled-integer arithmetic gives exact results for the general dyadic complex fixture. Both cover every subpixel bin, borders and points outside the logical image; the full padded storage and physical load range are checked. Native and CUDA.jl use warp shuffles. KA and JACC use a source-documented shared-memory emulation of that reduction dataflow, adding 4KB and block barriers. This is a selected portable mapping, not proof that either framework lacks all alternative shuffle implementations. Its timing cannot isolate the cost of the abstraction from the chosen reduction mapping without a controlled alternative and profiling.
effort_observation: One candidate and one complete compiler/JIT validation process per Julia model, with no observed compiler, runtime or numerical feedback repair. The historical CUDA.jl phase aligns precision and measurement inputs; no wrong-scientific-operator repair is claimed. Static mixed-precision binning and point-order scope findings are preserved separately from measured numerical outcomes.
